lead: `echo` writes its operands one at a time, so a throwing call in the middle of one leaves half a line on stdout.
body: `try { echo "[", $t, "] port=", Show::port($t), "\n"; } catch (Throwable $e) { echo "[", $t, "] refused\n"; }` prints `[x] port=[x] refused`, which reads as a subtly wrong expectation, and freezing it pins the prefix of every refused row. Bind the call to a local inside the `try` and echo the whole line after it — or route each verdict through one helper returning a `string`, which also lets verdicts be counted over a corpus.
